question: What will be the percentage change in front-month silver futures (SI=F on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-08-14 to the close on 2026-09-20?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-09-20 / close on 2026-08-14 - 1), using daily closes of SI=F on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-09-20, the last close before it is used.

research:
I couldn't confirm the official 2026-08-14 close. The best estimate is about $65 (the September contract). The question is not settled: the resolution close will most likely be Friday 2026-09-18, because 2026-09-20 falls on a Sunday.

## 1. Resolution source
- The source is Yahoo Finance SI=F daily closes. My fetch of the Yahoo history page was refused by the proxy, so **I could not read the official 2026-08-14 close**.
- 2026-08-14: Yahoo said the September contract opened at $64.63, down 0.6% from Thursday's close. That puts Thursday's close at about $65.0. Silver was $65.14 at 8:03 a.m. ET and $64.92 at 1:50 p.m. EDT. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/investing/article/silver-prices-today-friday-august-14-2026-silver-over-65-following-soft-inflation-data-this-week-121251820.html)
- 2026-08-14: Trading Economics said silver rebounded to about $65 on Friday, a weekly gain of more than 2%. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/silver/news/575505)
- Two points on mechanics:
  - Because 09-20 is a Sunday, the 09-18 close should be the one used.
  - SI=F will probably roll from the September to the December contract in late August, around first notice. December normally trades at a small premium (carry of roughly 0.5-1% at about 3.6% interest rates). That premium could add a small upward effect to the measured change that has nothing to do with the spot price. This is my inference; I did not check how Yahoo handles the roll.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. The starting price is about $65, and the price path through 09-18 is still open.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-14: Softer-than-expected US inflation data suggested that energy-price shocks from the Iran conflict eased in July. That lowers pressure on the Fed to tighten. The same report warns that new Middle East tension could push energy prices and inflation fears back up. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/silver/news/575505)
- 2026-08-13: An early-morning quote put silver at about $65.57, up about 1% from the prior settlement of about $64.94. It was up about 72% over the past year. [NaturalResourceStocks](https://naturalresourcestocks.net/silver-price-today-aug-13-2026/)
- 2026-08-10 (per a search summary): FXEmpire said the previous week's rally followed weak July payrolls (-23,000 jobs). [FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/silver-xag-forecast-cpi-determines-whether-silver-targets-74-63-or-retests-60-83-1615832)
- July 2026 FOMC: the Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote. All three dissenters wanted a rate **hike**. [FutureSearch](https://futuresearch.ai/app/p/a/will-the-u-s-federal-reserve-fomc-announce-a)

## 4. Base rates and volatility
- 2026-01-29/30: Silver hit a record near $121, then fell in a historic crash (the biggest one-day drop since 1982, per Reuters as cited). [Curaçao Chronicle](https://www.curacaochronicle.com/post/local/silver-market-experiences-extreme-volatility-in-2026-amid-geopolitical-tensions-and-supply-concerns), [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/precious-metals-witness-historic-crash-after-record-rally/79533.html)
- June 2026 average: $66.34. July 2026 average: $59.08, about 11% lower. [FindBullionPrices](https://www.findbullionprices.com/premium-history/silver-bars/1-oz-Silver-Bar-Random-Generic/)
- July 2026 ranged from a high of $62 (Jul 6) to a low of $55.33 (Jul 17). The last week of July went from $58.46 to $57.78. [Farms.com](https://www.farms.com/markets/commodity/silver-commodity-update-for-the-week-ending-jul-31-2026)
- So silver went from about $57.8 at the end of July to about $65 in mid-August, a rise of about 12% in two weeks. That shows how big short-term swings have been.
- My rough estimate of typical variation (not from a source): the window is about 25 trading days. In normal years silver's annualized volatility is 25-30%, which gives a 1-sigma move of about 8-9%. In 2026 realized volatility has been much higher, so a 1-sigma move of 10-15% looks plausible.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market for the Sept 18-20 close dated on or before 08-16.
- A Robinhood prediction market existed for the Aug 14 settlement, but it did not show the figure. [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/prediction-markets/metals/events/silver-price-august-14-2026-aug-14-2026/)
- Manifold has a market on the August 2026 silver futures price. I did not see its current odds. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/uair01/silver-futures-price-august-2026-be)
- As of 08-04, an illiquid Octagon market showed about 51% no change and 47% for a 25 bp hike at the September FOMC, with about 1-2% for a cut. [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/fomc/economic-policy/fed-decision-in-september.md)
- I found no bank forecasts for a 5-week horizon.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2026-09-18
- Late August: likely SI=F roll from the September to the December contract (see section 1).
- Late August: Jackson Hole symposium, plus the July PCE inflation data.
- Early September (probably 09-04): August jobs report. July's negative payrolls number lifted silver.
- Around 09-10/11: August CPI and PPI.
- 09-15/16: FOMC meeting. Most sources list these dates, but they conflict, so treat them as unconfirmed. A hike would weigh on silver.
- Ongoing: US-Iran tension and oil prices, which affect inflation fears, the dollar, and safe-haven demand.
